FOREWORD

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Travel, Tourism, and Hospitality Related Services Sectional Committee has been approved by the Service Sector Division Council.

Beaches are important natural assets that provide recreation, support tourism, and help coastal communities earn their livelihood. Beaches also protect marine ecosystems and biodiversity. With growing tourism and environmental awareness, it is essential to manage beaches in a manner that is environmentally friendly, socially inclusive, and economically beneficial.

Sustainable beach management requires a well-planned and responsible approach to their operation and maintenance. This standard has been developed to provide comprehensive framework for operation and management of beaches, with a focus on environmental protection, visitor safety and security, infrastructure, services and long-term ecological health.

The standard outlines key requirements for sustainable beach management, including providing environmental information, fostering stakeholder education and awareness, maintaining high standards of water quality, and promoting environmentally responsible practices. It also highlights the importance of safety, security, ecological conservation, and maintaining essential beach infrastructure and services.

By integrating these key elements, the standard aims to help authorities, operators and stakeholders in maintaining beaches that are safe, well managed, and environmentally responsible. It serves as a useful framework to improve beach quality, sustainability and user experience of beaches, ensuring these natural resources are protected for current and future generations.

This standard has been developed in alignment with national policies, environmental laws such as the Environmental Protection Act, Environmental Protection Rules 1986, Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, and Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) notifications, and insights from experts and practitioners in beach management and sustainable tourism.

The 42 requirements related to beach operations, covered under 6.1 to 6.7, are listed in Annex B.

SUSTAINABLE BEACH OPERATIONS — REQUIREMENTS


## 1 SCOPE

This standard specifies the requirements for the sustainable operation and maintenance of beach, focusing on key aspects essential to effective and responsible beach management. It addresses the following key aspects:

- a) Environmental information;
- b) Stakeholder education and awareness;
- c) Water quality assessment and management;
- d) Beach environment, management, and sustainable practices;
- e) Safety and security;
- f) Ecological conservation; and
- g) Beach infrastructure and services.

## 2 REFERENCES

The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions, which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent edition of these standards.

### 5.2  Operational Flag


5.2.1 The operational flag colour corresponding to the class of the beach shall be as specified below:

- a) Class I — Orange colour;
- b) Class II — Royal blue colour; and
- c) Class III — Green colour.

5.2.2 The construction, dimensions, and colour fastness of the operational flag shall comply with the requirements given in Annex D. The BMC shall arrange a test report of operational flag by a NABL accredited or government approved laboratory for compliance with the specified requirements as given in Annex D. The test reports of the flag issued by the laboratory shall be maintained.


5.2.3 The size of the operational flag shall be smaller than the dimensions of the National Flag.


5.2.4 The operational flag shall be inspected regularly and replaced immediately in case of fading, tearing, or any form of damage that reduces visibility or legibility.


5.2.5 The operational flag of the beach shall be hoisted/flown at a prominent location within the beach premises, such as near the main entrance, lifeguard station, or control point, at a height ensuring maximum visibility to visitors. The operational flag serves as a visual indicator of the classification status and compliance level of the beach.

### 6.4 Beach Environment, Management and Sustainable Practices


#### 6.4.1 Beach Suitability Assessment Study (BSAS)


6.4.1.1 To minimize erosion related risks, safeguard infrastructure, and promote ecologically responsible development, a Beach Suitability Assessment Study (BSAS) shall be conducted to ensure the long-term sustainability through comprehensive evaluation of the physical, environmental, and socio-economic parameters of the coastal area.


6.4.1.2 BSAS shall include the following:

- a) Assessment of land suitability for infrastructure development without encroaching upon ecologically sensitive areas, and ensuring compliance with the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) norms and other applicable national or regional regulations;
- b) Scientific analysis of shoreline dynamics, erosion trends, pollution levels, disaster vulnerability, and ecosystem integrity; and
- c) Structured consultations with local stakeholders, recognizing their essential role in sustainable development, conflict mitigation, and the long-term stewardship of coastal resources.

6.4.1.3 The information as given in Annex H, but not limited to, shall be collected during BSAS, prior to the development of the sustainable beach. All detailed findings and data obtained during BSAS shall be documented in the form of a report. On the basis of recommendations of the report, the BMC shall  initiate   the   development   of  the  sustainable

beach and ensure implementation of recommendations of the BSAS report.


#### 6.4.2 Environment Management Plan

The BMC shall prepare, document and implement an environment management plan (EMP) to ensure the protection, conservation, and sustainable use of coastal and marine ecosystems in and around the designated beach area. The EMP shall serve as a guiding framework for integrating environmental safeguards into all operational activities at the beach. The detailed framework and components of the Environment Management Plan are provided in Annex J.

#### 6.4.5 Solid Waste Management Facilities

The BMC shall be responsible for establishing and maintaining facilities for solid waste management through the following measures:

- a) Where municipal waste collection systems are unavailable or inaccessible near the beach area, establishment of solid waste treatment plant(s) (SWTPs) in close proximity to process and treatment of waste generated at the beach; and
- b) Provision of facilities for segregation of recyclable waste at source including separate collection systems for materials such as glass, plastic, paper, and metals.

#### 6.4.6 Restroom Facilities


6.4.6.1 The BMC shall determine and ensure availability of the number of toilets/restrooms (with well-maintained waste bins) for both males, and females, strategically located based on the beach area, and the number of major access points.


6.4.6.2 Toilet/restroom facilities shall be easily located through signage and accessible to visitors with special needs.

6.4.6.4 Restroom facilities shall be cleaned regularly to maintain high hygiene, with increased cleaning frequency during public holidays, weekends, and large public gatherings. The beach manager shall prepare and monitor a cleaning schedule for restroom/toilets.


#### 6.4.7 Access to Pets and Domestic Animals

The BMC shall prohibit the entry of pets and domestic animals on the beach. However, if the BMC has the policy/guidelines to permit the access to pet and domestic animals, such access shall be restricted to parking areas, walkways and promenades located within the inland portion of the beach area. The beach manager shall be responsible for preventing the entry of pet and domestic animals, and stray animals into the beach area. The public shall be made aware through signage or posters about the rules concerning pet and domestic animals.


#### 6.4.8 Access to Vehicles

The entry of vehicles to the beach shall be prohibited, except for those used for essential purposes such as cleaning operations, safety patrols including movement of lifeguard equipment, or emergency response. Where complete prohibition of vehicles is not feasible, the BMC shall have justification and documented guidelines to ensure safe and regulated vehicle movement in coordination with local authorities.

### 6.5 Ecological Conservation


#### 6.5.1 Marine Debris Management


6.5.1.1 The BMC shall monitor the accumulation of marine debris, including growth of seaweed, driftwood, and organic matter, regularly and inform the relevant environmental authority for management and removal whenever potential risk to public health is anticipated.


6.5.1.2 The BMC shall ensure that the removal of marine debris does not interfere with essential ecosystem functions, such as providing nutrients to beach vegetation or serving as habitat for marine



organisms. A balance shall be maintained between cleanliness and preserving ecological health to ensure the overall well-being of the beach environment.


#### 6.5.2 Conservation of Native Coastal Habitats

The BMC shall implement appropriate measures to safeguard native coastal habitats, including dunes, sea turtle nesting sites, and habitats of burrowing fauna such as crabs, sand dwellers and bird breeding areas to maintain biodiversity and ensure the long- term stability of coastal ecosystems. Buffer zones shall be established with clear signage to restrict visitors access to these sensitive habitats. The beach manager shall ensure limited and essential use of mechanical cleaning methods to avoid unintentional damage to sensitive habitats.


#### 6.5.3 Monitoring Measures for Ecological of Sensitive Area (ESA)

The BMC shall implement and monitor the protective measures for coastal ecosystems on the beach area, as given below:

- a) Protection of existing sand dunes using appropriate dune vegetation and fencing, recognizing their role in preventing beach erosion, replenishing beach sand, and supporting groundwater recharge;
- b) Installation of information billboards on or near sand dunes to highlight their ecological significance;
- c) Conservation of sea turtle nesting habitats by artificial lighting, and maintaining suitable environmental conditions, and promoting awareness among beach users;
- d) Protection of estuaries and mangrove ecosystems from land based pollution sources;
- e) Identification and protection of coral reef zones located near the beach at shallow depths (5 m to 20 m). Conduct baseline monitoring of coral reefs within 500 m from the beach and carry out coral reef health checks at least once annually;
- f) Maintenance, restoration and renovation of coastal archaeological sites, especially those of tourism importance and vulnerable to erosion and weathering; and
- g) Monitoring and reporting of illegal activities, including beach sand mining, mineral extraction (for example quartz and silicate), marine shell collection and, enforcement of bans and restrictions on such activities.

- f) Periodic drills shall be conducted at regular intervals to assess readiness and communication efficiency. The records of such drills shall be maintained.

#### 6.6.3 Emergency Preparedness


6.6.3.1 The BMC shall ensure the following for emergency preparedness:

- a) Establish, document, and implement an emergency response plan (ERP) in consultation with relevant stakeholders, such as the local administration, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), police, hospitals, fire department, State Pollution Control Board and State Departments of Environment;
- b) The ERP shall address mitigation measures for a wide range of potential incidents, including medical emergencies, extreme weather events, natural disasters, oil spills, hazardous waste spills, fires, pollution, and other critical situations;
- c) The EMP shall clearly define procedures, roles, and public warning and information systems to facilitate prompt and effective action in the case of an emergency; and
- d) The emergency plan shall be documented and reviewed at regular intervals for its revision, if needed. The records of review of the emergency plan shall be maintained.
NOTE — The deployment of the beach lifeguard patrol vehicle equipped with a spine board, rescue and first aid equipment is also recommended.

6.6.3.2 The BMC shall conduct:

- a) joint emergency drills at least once in a year, involving all relevant agencies and stakeholders, to ensure that all parties are aware of their respective roles and responsibilities during emergency situations; and
- b) regular training(s), time to time on need basis focusing on stakeholders, the operation of rescue equipment, administration of first aid, and execution of evacuation protocols. The records of all training shall be maintained.
NOTE — The BMC should deploy a beach lifeguard patrol vehicle equipped with a spine board, rescue equipment, and first aid supplies to support rapid and effective emergency response.


#### 6.6.4 Management of User Conflict Zone

The BMC shall:

- a) establish and maintain clearly demarcated zones for various beach activities to minimize user conflicts. These zones shall include designated and signposted areas for swimming, surfing, water sports, fishing, and other permitted activities, ensuring safe and uninterrupted enjoyment for all visitors;
- b) display information boards at prominent locations to inform visitors about various demarcated activity zones and designated areas, ensuring that all beach users are aware of permitted activities, behavioural expectations, and boundaries; and
- c) regularly monitor beach activities, particularly in areas prone to user conflict. The visitor feedback, on-site observations, and incident reports shall be utilized to update and improve beach management strategies accordingly.

- c) ensure that all emergency alarm systems are with backup power; and
- d) conduct periodic awareness campaigns through digital platforms, on-site signage, and live demonstrations, to educate beach users on how to respond when an alarm is triggered.

#### 6.6.7 Risk Assessment for Beach Operations

The BMC shall:

- a) identify and validate safe bathing zones based on comprehensive assessments of natural coastal factors. These assessments shall be primarily governed by the bathymetry (underwater topography) of the coastal waters, hydrodynamics, coastal currents, rip currents, wave parameters, and tidal variations;
- b) evaluate wave patterns to ensure that waves, break parallel to the shoreline are designated safe for bathing; and
- c) identify zones with mild, parallel currents, as they aid in dispersing pollutants and reducing water stagnation. Zones prone to rip currents shall be closely monitored and clearly demarcated as restricted for all bathing or water sports activities to ensure public safety.
NOTE — The identification and validation of safe bathing zones shall be based on comprehensive environmental, hydrodynamic, and water quality assessments.

### 6.7 Beach Infrastructure and Services


#### 6.7.1 Drinking Water

The BMC shall ensure the provision of safe and clean drinking water within accessible areas of the beach. The following measures shall be undertaken:

- a) Drinking water facilities shall be conveniently located and easily accessible to all visitors;
- b) Water purifiers or filtration systems shall be installed at all designated points; and
- c) Water testing shall be conducted at regular intervals preferably not exceeding six months, to ensure compliance with IS 10500.

#### 6.7.2 Electricity Arrangements

The BMC shall ensure the safe and reliable provision of electricity at the beach premises and shall take the following measures:

- a) Install concealed and insulated electrical wiring;
- b) Regular inspection and maintenance electrical appliances and installations;
- c) Install an electricity supply backup system;
- d) Ensure proper earthing of all electrical systems, equipment and appliances for human safety;




- e) Secure and restrict access to areas housing electrical infrastructure to prevent unauthorized handling; and
- f) Install renewable energy solutions, such as solar power systems, where feasible.
NOTE — Ensure installation of electrical products as per Indian Standards, wherever applicable.


#### 6.7.3 Lighting

The BMC shall ensure the following:

- a) Provisions of an adequate and well distributed lighting system across the beach area to ensure safety and visibility during low light conditions; and
- b) Promotion and utilization of renewable energy powered lighting systems.

#### 6.7.4 Administrative Facilities

The BMC shall provide and maintain appropriate administrative infrastructure to support effective beach management, including the following:

- a) Provision of administrative offices to efficiently support staff operations and coordination;
- b) Provision of dedicated space and staff for reception areas to assist and address visitor’s queries;
- c) Establish and implement adequate security measures, including access control systems in administrative areas;
- d) Ensure the establishment and implementation of procedures for visitor registration and maintenance of record; and
- e) Arrangements for displaying the emergency contact numbers such as beach emergency number, police, nearest hospital, and fire services at prominent locations across beach facilities.

Ensure the establishment and implementation of procedures for visitor registration and maintenance of record; and
- e) Arrangements for displaying the emergency contact numbers such as beach emergency number, police, nearest hospital, and fire services at prominent locations across beach facilities.

#### 6.7.5 CCTV Camera

The BMC shall ensure the installation and continuous operation of CCTV surveillance systems to enhance safety and security across the beach area. The following provisions shall be implemented:

- a) Install CCTV cameras at strategic locations and ensure a clear view of potential risk zones without compromising visitor privacy;
- b) All camera feeds shall be monitored in real-time by trained personnel to enable prompt response to any incidents;

- c) Ensure prompt action in response to any incident including theft, vandalism, or emergencies;
- d) CCTV footage shall be securely stored for a duration in accordance with applicable local laws, regulations, or government orders/guidelines, where such provisions are not specified, the BMC shall define the retention period. Measures shall be in place to prevent unauthorized access to CCTV footage and stored data; and
- e) Display information at prominent places regarding the presence and placement of CCTV cameras to maintain transparency and address privacy concerns.
NOTE — It is recommended to use AI-enabled cameras to identify potential emergencies and provide automated alerts.


#### 6.7.6 Communication

The BMC shall ensure the availability of communication systems across the beach premises to facilitate operations and emergency response. The following provisions for communication shall apply:

- a) Install communication facilities such as telephone lines for internal and external communication at appropriate locations;
- b) Determine and provide additional communication infrastructure including computers, internet, teleconferencing facilities, walkie-talkie sets, public address system (PA system) as required;
- c) Ensure that mobile phones are provided to key personnel, particularly those responsible for security and emergency coordination within the beach area; and
- d) Display phone numbers of key officials and essential services prominently across the beach area for public awareness and quick access during emergencies.

#### 6.7.7 Waste Disposal Bins/Containers

The BMC shall ensure the availability of adequately placed, secure, and well maintained waste disposal bins/containers across the beach as specified below:


##### 6.7.7.1 Waste segregation

Colour-coded bins shall be provided to facilitate segregation of waste into at least three categories:

- a) General waste;
- b) Recyclables; and
- c) Organic waste.



All bins shall be clearly labelled in English, Hindi and the local language, fitted with secure lids, and designed to be tamper proof and resistant to animals, where needed.


##### 6.7.7.2 Strategic placement

The bins shall be installed at strategic and high use locations, including, but not limited to:

- a) Entrances and exits;
- b) Restrooms and toilet facilities;
- c) Parking and recreational areas; and
- d) Food courts, seating zones, and other congregation points.

##### 6.7.7.3 Bin material

The bins shall be made of eco-friendly, weather- resistant, and durable materials, and should align with the aesthetic and environmental principles of sustainable beach management.


##### 6.7.7.4 Capacity and collection frequency

The capacity, number and placement of each bin, as well as the frequency of waste collection, shall be determined based on the expected visitor numbers, especially during peak tourist seasons, to prevent overflow and littering.


##### 6.7.7.5 Maintenance and monitoring

The BMC shall ensure regular inspection, cleaning, and timely emptying of all bins. Overflowing, damaged and malfunctioning bins shall be immediately addressed. Maintenance activities shall be documented and monitored to ensure compliance.

NOTE — Solid waste shall include, but is not limited to, solid or semi-solid domestic waste, sanitary waste, commercial and institutional waste, market and catering waste, street sweepings, drain silt, horticulture and agricultural waste, and other such non-residential or treated wastes as defined under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016.

#### 6.7.15 Cloakroom

To enhance visitor convenience and ensure the secure storage of personal belongings, the BMC shall provide a well-maintained cloakroom facility within the beach premises, with the following provisions:

## ANNEX E

(Clause 6.2.1.4)

BEACH EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES

E-1 The BMC shall undertake the following activities related to awareness, education, and training:

- a) Organize educational and awareness activities on the beach involving all beach stakeholders including local communities, visitors, school groups, and tourism operators to promote sustainable tourism and responsible beach use;
- b) Conduct active awareness initiatives such as guided tours, educational games, theatre performance or plays, and community beach cleaning campaigns;
- c) Conduct passive awareness initiatives including exhibitions, films, brochures, pamphlets, presentations, leaflets, posters, interpretive signage, newsletters, postcards, stickers, books, T-shirts, bags, and radio broadcasts;
- d) Organize and conduct targeted training programmes for key personnel including teachers, beach staff, individuals in charge of children’s groups, lifeguards, cleaners, and law enforcement officials;
- e) Implement community awareness and environmental education initiatives through a designated beach environmental information centre, where informative materials, exhibitions, and interactive sessions can be hosted for diverse groups; and
- f) Design and deliver specific awareness programmes, such as children’s awareness programmes on the importance of a safe and clean beach environment (minimum duration of 2 hours) and seminars covering key environmental issues and mitigation measures (recommended duration of half- day sessions).

## ANNEX F

(Clause 6.3.1.1)

CALCULATION OF THE 95th PERCENTILE

F-1 The microbiological monitoring data shall be evaluated using a log₁₀ normal probability density function to derive upper percentile values (used for classification and risk assessment). The following procedure shall be used:

- a) Convert each microbial count to its log₁₀ value. For zero values, use the log₁₀ of the detection limit of the test method;
b) Calculate the arithmetic mean of the log₁₀ values (μ); and


c) Calculate the standard deviation of the log₁₀ values (σ).


The upper percentiles shall be calculated as:

a) upper 90 percentile = antilog (μ + 1.282 σ); and


b) upper 95 percentile = antilog (μ + 1.645 σ).

(Clause 6.4.2)

J-1 The environmental management plan shall be prepared to include criteria, but not be limited to, the following:

- a) Conservation and protection measures to safeguard flora and fauna, including turtle nesting and fish spawning areas;
- b) Conservation plan for migratory species, critically endangered species or other protected species; and
- c) Conservation plan for habitats like mangroves, sand dunes, rocky, or marshy
habitats etc, to ensure that such habitats are not disturbed or cleared;
